options: A Fabric item that ingests a continuous flow of events and routes them, on a visual canvas, meant to stay running indefinitely
A one-time batch job that runs and then stops
A feature only available inside a Warehouse item
A synonym for a Fabric pipeline's Copy activity
questions.explain: Where a pipeline runs and finishes, an Eventstream is meant to stay running, the same "always on" idea from Structured Streaming's processingTime trigger.

questions.q: What are the three kinds of nodes an Eventstream is built from?
options: Workspace, capacity, and item
Notebook, pipeline, and semantic model
Source, transformation, and destination
Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Dataflow
questions.explain: Sources are where events come from, transformations reshape them in flight, and destinations are where they end up.

questions.q: Can a single Eventstream have more than one destination?
options: Only Warehouses can be used as destinations, never Lakehouses
Only if two separate Eventstreams are created
No, every Eventstream is limited to exactly one destination
Yes — the same stream can feed both an Eventhouse for real-time queries and a Lakehouse for later batch analysis, at once
questions.explain: This is a real, useful pattern — one ingestion point, multiple consumers.

questions.q: How does an Eventstream compare to Databricks & Delta Lake's Autoloader?
options: Conceptually the same job — automatically picking up new data without manual intervention — but for a continuous event stream instead of files landing periodically
Autoloader is for streaming, Eventstream is for batch files
They are functionally identical with no real difference
There's no meaningful comparison between the two
questions.explain: Autoloader's checkpoint tracks files; an Eventstream's engine tracks events in a stream that never technically finishes.

questions.q: What happens immediately after publishing an Eventstream?
options: It runs once and then stops, like a pipeline
It requires a separate scheduling step before it can start
It waits for a manual trigger before starting
It starts running immediately, continuously
questions.explain: This reflects the "always on" nature described earlier in the lesson.
